quotes.quote: Facing the machine, sit on the floor (or on the long seat pad, if available). Place the feet on the machine frame or foot supports. Flex the knees and hips to reach forward and grasp the handle with a closed, neutral grip.
Set up for the cable row is with your feet about hip width apart, knees slightly bent,chest is tall and pull the shoulders down and back
Pull the handle back and assume an erect seated position with the torso perpendicular to the floor, knees slightly flexed, and the feet and legs parallel to each other.
Allow the elbows to fully extend with the arms about parallel to the floor.
The handle should finish at your stomach, keeping a nice straight line.
Touch the handle to the sternum or abdomen.
Flex (bend) your elbows and pull them towards your chest keeping your elbows close to the sides of your body.
Continue pulling until your elbows pass the sides of your body.
Maintain an erect torso position with the knees in the same slightly flexed position.
Keeping your body still, pull the elbows straight back
Allow the elbows to slowly extend back to the starting position.
Return to the start position, fully extending the arms and without leaning forward.
Jerking the upper body or leaning back during the backward movement phase
Curling the handle toward the torso during the backward movement phase
Flexing the torso forward during the forward movement phase
Avoid leaning back and arching your low back
Additionally, reduce unnecessary stresses into your low back by avoiding any backwards lean during the pull movements.
maintain a neutral wrist position (i.e., wrist in line with your forearms) and attempt to hold these positions throughout the exercise.
pull the shoulders down and back so they're stacked in your backpockets.
Maintain your upright trunk position and avoid forward rounding of your scapulae (shoulder blades).
Pause momentarily then slowly return to your starting position, allowing your arms to move forward and elbows to extend (straighten) in a slow, controlled manner
Allow the elbows to slowly extend back to the starting position.
